routes.label: Find the base using special right triangles

question:
In rectangle \(ABCD,\) \(DC = 2 \cdot CB\) and points \(E\) and \(F\) lie on \(\overline{AB}\) so that \(\overline{ED}\) and \(\overline{FD}\) trisect \(\angle ADC\) as shown. What is the ratio of the area of \(\triangle DEF\) to the area of rectangle \(ABCD?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2014_AMC_10B_Q15_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The triangle and rectangle have the same height, so finding the length of \(EF\) will let us compare their areas. Let \(AD=h>0\). Opposite sides of the rectangle are equal, so \(AB=DC=2h\).

The trisectors divide the right angle at \(D\) into three \(30^\circ\) angles. Thus \(\angle ADE=30^\circ\) and \(\angle ADF=60^\circ\). A \(30^\circ\)-\(60^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) triangle has side ratio \(1:\sqrt3:2\): its hypotenuse is twice its short leg, and the Pythagorean theorem gives the long leg.

In right triangle \(ADE\), \(AD\) is the long leg; in right triangle \(ADF\), it is the short leg. Therefore
\[
AE=\frac{h}{\sqrt3},\qquad AF=\sqrt3h.
\]
Since the figure places \(E\) between \(A\) and \(F\),
\[
EF=AF-AE=\frac{2h}{\sqrt3}.
\]
The altitude from \(D\) to the line \(EF\) has length \(h\). Consequently,
\[
\frac{[DEF]}{[ABCD]}
=\frac{\tfrac12 EF\cdot h}{AB\cdot h}
=\frac{EF}{2AB}
=\frac{2h/\sqrt3}{4h}
=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt3}{6}}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{A}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
The trisection also creates an equal-side relationship inside \(\triangle DEF\), allowing us to find \(EF\) directly. Let \(AD=h>0\), so \(AB=DC=2h\).

The trisectors give \(\angle EDF=30^\circ\) and \(\angle ADF=60^\circ\). Because \(AD\perp AB\), right triangle \(ADF\) has \(\angle AFD=30^\circ\). The points \(E\) and \(A\) lie on the same ray from \(F\), so \(\angle EFD=30^\circ\) as well. Equal angles in \(\triangle DEF\) have equal opposite sides, giving
\[
EF=DE.
\]
Now \(\triangle ADE\) is right with \(\angle ADE=30^\circ\), so \(AE=DE/2\). The Pythagorean theorem yields
\[
h^2=DE^2-AE^2
=DE^2-\frac{DE^2}{4}
=\frac34DE^2.
\]
Taking the positive length gives \(EF=DE=2h/\sqrt3\). Using \(EF\) as the triangle's base, its altitude is \(h\). Hence
\[
\frac{[DEF]}{[ABCD]}
=\frac{\tfrac12(2h/\sqrt3)h}{(2h)h}
=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt3}{6}}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
